### Confirming in 1.18.x — and the blast radius is much larger than "a 400 on message GET"

Reproducing this on opencode **1.18.x** (server) today, but via the most common real‑world trigger: the [`opencode-claude-memory`](https://github.com/kuitos/opencode-claude-memory) plugin, whose `recall-selector` agent sends exactly this `format` on every `session.prompt`:

```json
{
  "type": "json_schema",
  "schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": { "selected_memories": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } } },
    "required": ["selected_memories"],
    "additionalProperties": false
  },
  "retryCount": 2
}
```

The prompt is accepted, the LLM completes, but the server then rejects the persisted message on read‑back and **retries the whole structured‑output call in a tight loop** — indefinitely:

```
level=WARN message="schema rejection" kind=Body
reason="Expected OutputFormatJsonSchema, got {\"type\":\"json_schema\",\"schema\":{...},\"retryCount\":2}\n  at [0][\"info\"][\"format\"]"
```

#### Why this matters beyond a 400

1. **It's a runaway retry loop, not a one‑off rejection.** Each rejection retries every ~5 s, 24/7, for the life of the session. I measured **>1,600 `schema rejection` lines/hour** sustained over days from a single recall sub‑session — i.e. thousands of wasted LLM calls + a session that never goes idle. The original report stops at "GET returns 400"; the actual user‑visible behaviour is an infinite retry storm.
2. **It breaks the most popular memory plugin for everyone.** Any opencode install with `opencode-claude-memory` enabled hits this on every turn — recall is non‑fatal to the main conversation, but it silently burns quota and stalls the session. The plugin conforms to the SDK's `OutputFormatJsonSchema` exactly; the server's validator is the one out of sync.
3. **It cascades into downstream integrations.** I'm seeing this via `kimaki` (a Discord bridge over opencode): each stuck recall sub‑session gets mirrored into Discord as a `Sync:` thread, producing **hundreds of spam threads across every channel** + a bot stuck "typing…" forever. That downstream damage is what surfaced the bug for us — but it's a symptom of this same root cause.

#### Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** a `format` that the prompt endpoint accepts (and that matches `GET /doc`'s `OutputFormatJsonSchema`) round‑trips through `GET /session/:id/message` unchanged.
- **Actual:** the message‑listing deserialiser rejects its own persisted shape (`Expected OutputFormatJsonSchema, got {"type":"json_schema",...}`) and the caller retries forever.

#### Environment

- opencode `1.18.x` (server, via `kimaki` → opencode SDK), Windows + the in‑process plugin path.
- Triggering client: `@opencode-ai/sdk` `session.prompt` with `format: { type: "json_schema", ... }` (the recall‑selector pattern).

#### Fix

#37541 addresses exactly this — it changes the `OutputFormat*` schemas in `packages/schema/src/v1/session.ts` so persisted formats are encoded with a stable identifier and round‑trip cleanly, and adds a `returns persisted output formats` test covering the `json_schema` case. From reading the diff it should close both the HTTP‑API 400 **and** the in‑process retry loop reported here (same root cause: the persisted format losing its schema identifier on read‑back). Could this get some review eyes? The retry‑loop + quota‑burn angle makes it higher priority than the issue title suggests — every `opencode-claude-memory` user is affected.

Commenting to give this some eyes — and because I believe it closes a severity angle that isn't obvious from the linked issue (#26929).

I'm hitting #26929 via the in-process plugin path (the `opencode-claude-memory` `recall-selector` agent, which sends `format: { type: "json_schema", schema: {...}, retryCount: 2 }` on every `session.prompt`). In that path the rejection isn't a one-off HTTP 400 — the SDK call **retries in a tight loop** (every ~5 s, >1,600/hour, indefinitely), burning LLM quota and stalling the session. Full repro + the runaway-retry + downstream-cascade detail: [issue #26929 comment](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/26929#issuecomment-5263045157).

From reading this diff, the root cause it targets — the persisted `OutputFormat*` losing its schema identifier on read-back, so the deserialiser rejects its own persisted shape — is exactly what drives both the HTTP 400 **and** the retry loop (the loop is just the caller re-prompting after each failed read-back). So the added `returns persisted output formats` test covering `json_schema` is the right coverage.

Two questions / possible nits for the maintainer:

1. Does this also cover the **in-process** call site (not just the HTTP `/session/:id/message` endpoint)? The retry loop I'm seeing is via the SDK against the running server, not a raw HTTP GET — want to make sure the encoding fix lands on the shared serialisation path both use.
2. The `retryCount` field — worth confirming it round-trips too (the recall-selector format sets `retryCount: 2`), since the test asserts the full `format` object back.

If both check out, this looks mergeable as-is and would unblock every `opencode-claude-memory` user. Happy to test a build against the recall-selector repro if that'd help move it forward.

**Root cause narrowed + workaround confirmed**

The regression is specific to plugin tools registered with `options: { codemode: true }`:

- **`codemode: true`**: the tool appears in the CodeMode agent catalog, but (a) message-level direct invocation fails with `Unknown tool`, and (b) CodeMode `execute()` code-path invocation executes the tool server-side (side effects confirmed) while the result relays back as `undefined`.
- **`codemode: false`**: the tool leaves the CodeMode catalog/tree (expected behavior), and message-level direct invocation works correctly — both text results and file attachments relay fully.

So the `codemode: true` plugin-tool path has two breaks: dispatch resolution and result relay. `codemode: false` is a viable workaround — the tools then work through the normal provider tool-call path.

Hi @yiyinideshang, I'm experiencing a very similar "Edit Project save not taking effect" issue, and I'd like to add a reproduction from a **different runtime mode and platform** that may help isolate the root cause.

## Environment

- **OpenCode version**: 1.18.15 (npm global, `opencode-ai@1.18.15`)
- **Plugin version**: `@opencode-ai/plugin@1.16.2`
- **OS**: Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200)
- **Browser**: Microsoft Edge (Chromium)
- **Runtime mode**: `opencode web` (web UI, **not** the Desktop Electron client)
- **Project type**: Local directory project already present in the opencode project list, without an independent `project` table record (likely falling back to the `global` row)
- **Local config**: Multiple providers (deepseek, minimax, nvidia, sensenova, etc.), plugins `oh-my-opencode-slim` + TUI plugin. Storage: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (SQLite, WAL mode).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start with `opencode web` and open the web UI.
2. Right-click the target project in the project list -> **Edit Project**.
3. Change the **project name** to a new value and click **Save**.
4. Re-open the dialog - the name has **reverted to the original value**.

The **icon/color** shows the same behavior: selecting a new accent color -> Save -> reopen dialog shows **no selection / reverts to default**.

## Relation to the analysis in this issue

The save-branch logic described here - `if (props.project.id && id !== "global") { ...project.update(...) } else { sync.project.meta(worktree, {...}) }` - matches my observation closely: my project falls into the "no independent project table record, falls back to global row" category, so it takes the `else` branch and writes to the workspace `.dat` file rather than the `project` table in `opencode.db`.

I can also confirm the three points raised in #32691:
- No error is surfaced in the UI when saving (consistent with a missing `onError` on the mutation, silently swallowing API errors).
- The icon color appears to be submitted as `""` rather than an omitted field, resulting in no selected state on the next dialog open.
- No immediate UI refresh after save, as if relying on a delayed SSE event.

## Why this reproduction is useful

1. **First reported reproduction in `opencode web` mode.** All existing reports in #37345, #38478, and #32691 come from the Desktop client. If the web UI reproduces it too (as it does here), the root cause lives in the **shared backend persistence layer** rather than Desktop-specific rendering/sync paths.
2. **Independent confirmation on Windows**, ruling out a macOS-only trigger.
3. My configuration has **multiple providers and plugins**; reproduction under this setup helps rule out "only reproducible with minimal default config".

## Debug info I can provide (sanitized before sharing)

- Browser DevTools **Network/Console** capture of the Save request/response (request body fields, HTTP status, response body - can directly determine whether the backend receives the `name`/`color` fields).
- Sanitized excerpts from `opencode.workspace.<hash>.dat` and `opencode.global.dat`.
- Minimal screenshots of the reproduction, if needed.

Would it be helpful if I prioritize the Network request logs, to distinguish between "backend received but did not persist" (#37345 direction) versus "request silently failed" (#32691 direction)?

This also relates to #32691 and #38478; happy to move or consolidate if maintainers prefer a single tracker.

Thanks to the maintainers for the ongoing fixes, and thanks @yiyinideshang for the detailed analysis.

Adding a second consumer, and one failure class that isn't yet enumerated here.

We maintain bernstein, an Apache-2.0 orchestrator that runs CLI coding agents in
parallel git worktrees; OpenCode already ships as one of its adapters. We run:

    opencode run -m <model-id> --format json "<prompt>"

Beyond the provider-side failures above, there's a third class where the exit code is
actively misleading rather than merely undifferentiated: a run whose tool calls were
denied by the permission system exits 0. In packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts,
`error` is assigned only from `session.error` (L776-786) and consulted at L837; the
permission auto-reject path (L796-815) never sets it. #36413 reproduces this end to end.

The --format json stream doesn't close the gap either. It carries tool_use, step_start,
step_finish, text, reasoning, error (L720-784) but has no terminal event — the loop
breaks on session idle (L789-793) without emitting, so the stream just stops. A consumer
can't separate completion from abort, and has to infer totals by accumulating
step_finish parts.

So, a fourth option alongside the three above: emit a final event in the existing
envelope, at the point the loop already breaks.

    {"type":"result","sessionID":"ses_...","outcome":"success|error|blocked",
     "reason":"stop|length|tool-calls|aborted",
     "tokens":{"input":0,"output":0,"reasoning":0,"cache":{"read":0,"write":0}},
     "cost":0.0}

The values already exist at that point — step-finish carries reason, tokens and cost.
Consumers that ignore unknown types are unaffected, so it's additive.

Happy to send the PR. Would you prefer distinct exit codes, a terminal result event,
or both — and should result be gated behind --format json?

If any of this is already reachable and we've missed it, that answer alone unblocks us.

Thanks — the run.ts read matches what I see at HEAD, and the auto-reject branch never touching `error` explains why the exit 0 was 5/5 rather than intermittent. It isn't flaky, it's wired shut.

One refinement on the JSON channel, because I think the gap there is different from "can't separate blocked from finished" — and worse. A rejection *is* observable: the tool part is emitted with `state.status == "error"` and the rejection message, which is the workaround I'd been relying on. What's missing is a **completion marker**. `emit()` covers exactly `tool_use`, `step_start`, `step_finish`, `text`, `reasoning`, `error`; the loop then breaks on `session.status == idle` and returns without emitting. So the tail of a normally-finished stream is byte-identical to one whose process was killed, hit a timeout, or died mid-write.

That makes the third option in my original "Expected" list weaker than I wrote it: documenting "use `--format json` and inspect tool part states" does let you detect a rejection, but it still leaves a consumer unable to tell a complete run from a truncated one. So the ask narrows to the first two — a non-zero exit when a run ends with no assistant output because a tool was rejected, or a terminal event on the JSON stream (`session.idle` / `done`, with a reason). The latter fixes both at once and is the one I'd prefer.

>

Gated behind a new `model_override` permission that defaults to deny, so an agent can't silently move work to an expensive model; you allow patterns per provider in config (`"model_override": { "anthropic/*": "allow" }`). The permission check runs even on the `bypassAgentCheck` path — a task spawned by another task can't skip the ask.
> 
>     * **Resume keeps model and variant.** Resuming a `task_id` previously reverted the child to the agent default mid-conversation. The child session now records its last-used model/variant and resumes on it; an explicit `model` param still wins.
> 
>     * **Slug `task_id`s.** `task_id: "explore-auth"` creates a named child whose session id derives from sha256(slug + root session id), so the same slug from the same session tree resumes the same child. The slug also becomes the child session's display slug. Slugs are parent-scoped: using another session's slug errors instead of hijacking it.
> 
>     * **`variant` param** — per-dispatch reasoning preset (`"thinking"`, `"high"`, …). Unknown variants are ignored, same as the existing variant resolution. deepseek-v4 models additionally get a `none` variant that disables thinking (`{ thinking: { type: "disabled" } }`, same shape as the existing minimax-m3 `none` and identical to what agent-frontmatter `options.thinking` produces) — without it there was no per-dispatch way to run deepseek with thinking off, forcing a dedicated agent definition for what is one flag.
> 
>     * **`metadata` param** — opaque object stored on the child session row for plugins/queries. Shallow-merged on resume. Not shown to the subagent.
> 
>     * **`resume: true` gate.** Reusing a `task_id` that names an idle (finished) session used to silently continue it — an agent reusing a slug by accident inherits a stale context. Resuming an idle session now requires `resume: true`; a live background task still accepts follow-up prompts without it. This is the one behavior change in the PR.
> 
>     * **`timeout` + `fallback_model`** — bound a dispatch attempt in ms; optionally retry once on a different model when the attempt fails or times out. Fallback never fires on parent abort (interrupt) or defects, only typed failures. The retry cancels the child's prompt runner via a new `SessionRunState.cancelRun` rather than `cancel` — full cancel tears down the enclosing background job itself (job id == child session id), which killed the fallback before it could run.

Thanks — the gateway in my repro is LiteLLM exposing an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint and forwarding to OpenAI GPT-5.5.

The upstream rejection is specifically from OpenAI, not a LiteLLM-only validation rule:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "unsupported_parameter",
    "message": "Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model. Use 'max_completion_tokens' instead.",
    "param": "max_tokens",
    "type": "invalid_request_error"
  }
}
```

So for this provider path, `max_tokens` is not allowed. The upstream expects `max_completion_tokens`.

The important distinction from #22623 is the runtime path:

- #22623 sounds like Azure/native provider handling.
- This issue reproduces on the default AI SDK fallback path for an `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider.
- In that path, opencode calls `streamText({ maxOutputTokens: ... })`.
- `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` serializes that as `max_tokens`.
- OpenAI GPT-5.x rejects it before generation starts.

I verified a local mitigation:

```ts
model.api.npm === "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible" &&
/(?:^|\/)gpt-5(?:[.-]|$)/.test(model.api.id) &&
!model.api.id.includes("gpt-5-chat")
```

For that case, clearing `prepared.params.maxOutputTokens` prevents AI SDK from emitting `max_tokens`, and the request no longer fails at admission.

I also tested the native `@opencode-ai/llm` OpenAI Chat path separately: it needs to emit `max_completion_tokens` instead of `max_tokens` for `gpt-5*` chat-completions models.

So the two fixes I validated locally are:

1. AI SDK fallback / `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`: omit `maxOutputTokens` for GPT-5.x so AI SDK does not send `max_tokens`.
2. Native OpenAI Chat route: send `max_completion_tokens` for GPT-5.x instead of `max_tokens`.

Targeted tests I used locally:

```text
cd packages/opencode && bun test test/provider/transform.test.ts --timeout 30000
cd packages/llm && bun test test/provider/openai-chat.test.ts --timeout 30000
```

Both pass with the patch.

Follow-ups from the full event-handling parity audit (TUI vs desktop, every event in `packages/schema/src/event-manifest.ts`). Commit `7674941aad` fixed the four desktop gaps: the dead `filesystem.changed` listener, notifications keyed to the unpublished `session.idle`, the unreachable `project.directories.updated` handler, and the MCP-gated `command.updated` reload. The rest is tracked here.

**1. Go-upsell and rate-limit dialogs are dead on V2 (server design needed)**
`packages/app/src/pages/session/usage-exceeded-dialogs.tsx:54` subscribes to `session.status` with `status.retry.action`. No V2 publisher exists, and `session.retry.scheduled` (`packages/schema/src/session-event.ts:513-522`) carries only `assistantMessageID`, `attempt`, `at`, `error`. The upsell action payload (`free_tier_limit` / `account_rate_limit`, title, message, link) does not exist anywhere in the V2 schema or core. Porting requires the server to publish that data; the app code stays dormant until then.

**2. TUI gaps (separate PR)**
- `session.forked`: no handler anywhere in `packages/tui/src`. Fork publishes only `session.forked`, not `session.created` (`packages/core/src/session.ts:402-433`), so a fork made from another client does not appear in the TUI until a resync.
- `session.skill.activated`: handled only by the session-scoped mini transport (`packages/tui/src/mini/stream-v2.transport.ts:998`); the main reducer in `packages/tui/src/context/data.tsx` has no case, so the live transcript misses the row.
- `project.directories.updated`: no TUI handler; new sandbox/copy directories appear only after reconnect.
- `integration.connection.updated`: no TUI case; currently benign because core always pairs it with `integration.updated` (`packages/core/src/integration.ts:424-425, 480-481, 714-731`), but the pairing is an implicit contract.

**3. Desktop pty parity (feature-level)**
`packages/app/src/context/terminal.tsx:239` handles only `pty.exited`. `pty.created`, `pty.updated`, and `pty.deleted` are ignored, so terminals created, retitled, or removed by another client do not sync.

**4. Dead app code cleanup (small follow-up PR)**
- `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/event-reducer.ts:40-61`: `global.disposed` and `project.updated` have no V2 publisher and are not in `ServerDefinitions`.
- `server.instance.disposed` case in `applyDirectoryEvent` (`event-reducer.ts:125`): no such V2 event.
- The global-branch refetches for `config.updated` / `agent.updated` / `project.directories.updated` in `packages/app/src/context/server-sync.tsx:566-571` are unreachable: those events carry a location and never route to the `"global"` branch (`packages/app/src/context/server-sdk.tsx:170`).

**5. Server: undeclared 204 during location boot**
`/api/agent` (and possibly sibling routes) answers `204` before the location finishes booting. The generated client declares only 200/400/401 (`packages/client/src/promise/generated/client.ts:417-418`) and throws `UnexpectedStatus`. This was the root of the agent-dropdown race fixed in `c2777d4733`; a declared readiness status (e.g. 503 with retry semantics) or blocking until boot would remove this class for every client.

Both findings are addressed in 37749492a1.

**Finding 1 (process-wide EPIPE suppression):** accepted, with scoping as the achievable granularity. The process-level `uncaughtException`/`unhandledRejection` EPIPE handlers moved out of the shared entry into `guardServiceProcess()`, installed only by `serve --service` during service startup (`server-process.ts`). Foreground commands, `serve` without `--service`, and `--stdio` mode get no process-wide suppression. Source-level attribution is not possible for this failure: the crashing EPIPE arrives from native async write completion with an empty JS stack (`UNCAUGHT uncaughtException EPIPE: broken pipe, write`, no frames), so no owner in this repo can observe it. The true owner fix is upstream in the effect spawner, which detaches its child-stdin error listener once the write sink completes; a late EPIPE then has no listener and becomes an unhandled exception. Until that lands, the service-mode catch-all is the only mitigation, and it preserves fatal semantics (print and exit 1) for every non-EPIPE error. On the incomplete-operation concern: in the observed git case the owning Effect completes through the child exit-code path regardless, so the stray write completion carries no result anyone waits on.

**Finding 2 (foreground commands continuing after stdout closes):** accepted, and note the swallow-and-continue behavior for stdout predates this PR (the Node wrapper guard from 42e2dde739 did the same). The stream guard now applies mode-dependent policy: in foreground, an EPIPE on stdout terminates the process cleanly, so `opencode2 run "large task" | head -n 1` stops instead of continuing the model request; stderr EPIPE stays non-fatal as diagnostics. In service mode both streams are non-fatal, since a detached service's logging consumer may legitimately outlive or predecease it.

Validation: the desktop background service (the invocation that reproducibly crashed during its boot project-copy refresh under concurrent git activity) survives with the scoped guard, confirmed by a detached run completing `project copy refresh done` and by a live desktop session with no event-stream disconnect spam. Typecheck clean in `packages/cli`.

Two completed prompts in one fresh TUI lifecycle produced 70 `ALSA lib` lines total (35 per completion), with `default`, `dmix`, `dmix:0`, and `dmix:0,0` each attempted twice. That confirms repeated audio startup attempts on this build.

I also tried the requested timeline plugin. Placing it at `~/.config/opencode/plugins/attention-timeline.ts` caused the server plugin loader to claim it and reject it (`Missing key at ["default"]["effect"]` / `["default"]["setup"]`), so no timeline file was created. In this next-channel build, TUI plugins are discovered under `plugins/tui/`, and the runtime ABI had changed from `{ id, tui(api) }` to `{ id, setup(context) }`; events are exposed through `context.data.listen(...)` as `{ name, details }`.

OpenCode auto-updated while I investigated this from `next-17155` to `next-17288`. I adapted the plugin at `~/.config/opencode/plugins/tui/attention-timeline.ts` and mapped the current event names (`form.created`, `permission.asked`, `session.execution.succeeded`, `session.execution.failed`, and `session.step.failed`) to the four requested families. It loaded successfully, and a completion recorded:

```text
2026-08-12T11:16:45.098Z session.status session=ses_… parent=- status=idle source=session.execution.succeeded
```
